speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your symptoms in detail: how long have you had the persistent vomiting and chest pain, and what do you think might be causing them?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Serum Amylase/Lipase and Liver Function Panel.  
Do you recall if you felt something get stuck in your esophagus or throat right before the choking and coughing began?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture). The combination of forceful vomiting following alcohol consumption, followed by retching, choking, and subsequent chest pain, along with normal amylase/lipase levels (ruling out acute pancreatitis as the primary cause), is highly suggestive of a full-thickness tear of the esophagus. I am requesting a Chest X-Ray and a CT scan of the chest with contrast to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay, CT_Chest_With_Contrast.
